Resolution uses the strict first 2025-Q4 print without correction-day or revision exceptions."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch recent observations from BLS BED Table 1.","result":"BLS reports opening-establishment gross job gains of 1,589 thousand in 2025 Q1, 1,527 thousand in Q2, and 1,597 thousand in Q3, seasonally adjusted."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetch the pre-2025 reference class from BLS BED Table 1.","result":"The 2024 quarterly values were 1,531, 1,561, 1,564, and 1,660 thousand; the 2023 values were 1,570, 1,608, 1,586, and 1,637 thousand."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Check related total gross job gains and the official release schedule.","result":"Total private gross job gains were 7,448 thousand in 2025 Q1, 7,585 thousand in Q2, and 7,475 thousand in Q3; the BLS calendar schedules the 2025 Q4 BED release for July 29, 2026 at 10:00 AM."},{"kind":"text","text":"The outside-view base rate is the recent 2023-Q1 through 2025-Q3 reference class: opening-establishment gains have centered near 1.585 million, while the two latest Q4 observations were higher at 1.637 million and 1.660 million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level and momentum point in different directions: the series remains near 1.6 million and rebounded 70 thousand in Q3, but total gross gains eased from 7.585 million to 7.475 million. Recent Q4 strength supports an elevated anchor, while the softer 2025 labor-flow backdrop warrants a modest downward adjustment. No discrete policy or identifiable one-off mechanism justifies a larger shift."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: A recent-Q4 persistence model uses the 2023-Q4 and 2024-Q4 average, (1,637 + 1,660) / 2 = 1,648.5 thousand, based on the 11-quarter 2023-Q1–2025-Q3 historical sample. Apply a -13.5 thousand adjustment for softer 2025 total gross gains, giving 1,635.0. Because this is a flow series, dispersion is computed from the values themselves: sample sigma = 40.7 thousand. The normal 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 1.28*40.7 = 52.1 thousand, implying 1,635 ± 52, or final bounds of 1,583 to 1,687 thousand."},{"kind":"text","text":"Upside risk comes from another Q4 opening surge comparable to or stronger than 2024 and would land above the interval if the first print exceeds 1,687 thousand. Downside risk comes from broad-based establishment-formation weakness or reversal of the Q3 rebound and would land below the interval if the print is under 1,583 thousand."},{"kind":"forecast","point":1635,"ciLow":1583,"ciHigh":1687}]}
